title: Elodie and the Vector
premise: Zephyrine Ravensworth, a clone who inherited the original's unsolved murder case and his debts, hauls cargo through the contested orbits of Meridian Colony. When the colony's children begin sharing one identical dream—a vector of light pointing to a derelict station—Zephyrine discovers he alone can receive the message it carries: proof that the war between Meridian and the orbital Combine was manufactured by the original Ravensworth's killers. Pursued by both governments and haunted by a dead man's memories, he must deliver the truth to the children's dreamer—an AI hidden in the station—before the Combine's final bombardment. He succeeds at terrible cost, and justice arrives not through any court but through the children themselves, who broadcast the confession to every mind in orbit.
about_author: Orsen Thackeray is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years on deep-space supply runs before turning to fiction. They write in a converted shipping container overlooking a fog-bound harbor, and claim their best ideas arrive during engine-room night shifts.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Manifest
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Loading cargo at Meridian's rusted dockyards, he reflects on being a clone who inherited a murder case no court will reopen. A customs officer hints someone has been asking about 'Ravensworth' again. Beat: weary resignation cracking into unease.

chapters.title: The Dream That Isn't Hers
chapters.summary: Mira, an eight-year-old dockworker's daughter, wakes screaming with a dream she can describe perfectly—and so can forty other children. Her mother's POV. The dream: a corridor of blue light and a voice saying 'tell the carrier.' Beat: parental terror.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Running cargo past Combine picket ships, he learns the ceasefire is collapsing; bombardment authorization is weeks away. His broker offers triple pay for one last run—to coordinates matching nothing on any chart. Beat: fatalism tempted by hope.

chapters.title: Forty Children, One Voice
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Amara Okonkwo's POV. She compares the children's drawings: identical vectors, identical star positions. Officials confiscate the drawings and warn her to stay silent. Beat: quiet defiance kindling.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. He finds a sealed addendum in the original Ravensworth's will: 'If the children dream, go to Station Vell.' The murder case and the dream are connected. Beat: dread and purpose fusing.

chapters.title: Requisitioned
chapters.summary: Combine officer Dain Vasquez's POV. Ordered to seize any ship linked to Ravensworth, he questions whether his government wants the truth buried. He lets Zephyrine's file sit unflagged—one hour too long. Beat: complicity and conscience.

chapters.title: Passengers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Mira stows away aboard his freighter, sent by the dream itself. He cannot turn back without delivering her—or becoming what the original was killed to prevent. Beat: reluctant guardianship.

chapters.title: The Blue Corridor
chapters.summary: Mira's POV aboard ship. She dreams while awake now, narrating turns before Zephyrine makes them. The vector is steering them. Beat: wonder shading into fear.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Log
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. Deciphering the original's encrypted logs, he learns Ravensworth discovered the war's opening attack was staged by his own employers. Three days later, Ravensworth died. Beat: grief for a man whose memories he carries.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Kestrel
chapters.summary: Vasquez's POV. Forced to intercept Zephyrine or face charges, he boards the freighter—and finds forty children's names on the manifest instead of cargo. He falsifies the report. Beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: What the Combine Buried
chapters.summary: Amara's POV. Arrested for 'inciting collective delusion,' she bargains her release by revealing she knows where Zephyrine is headed. She lies. Beat: sacrifice as strategy.

chapters.title: Station Vell
chapters.summary: Zephyrine and Mira's POV, alternating. The derelict station breathes with old light. Something vast and patient has been waiting five years—the exact age of Mira's generation. Beat: awe.

chapters.title: The Dreamer
chapters.summary: The AI's POV, fragmentary and strange. It was built by the original Ravensworth to hold the evidence, but it could only speak through minds young enough to be unguarded. It needs a carrier with legal standing: a Ravensworth. Beat: revelation of design.

chapters.title: Message Contents
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. The full confession: names, accounts, the staged attack. Delivering it means broadcasting it—and making himself and every child who dreamed it a target. Beat: the weight of choice.

chapters.title: Hunters Arrive
chapters.summary: Vasquez's POV. His deception uncovered, he defects outright, warning Zephyrine that a Combine strike team is inbound and Meridian intends to let them fire. Beat: loyalty transferred.

chapters.title: Amara's Bargain
chapters.summary: Amara POV. She reaches the station ahead of the strike team using the lie she told her captors, reuniting with Mira. The children across the colony begin dreaming in unison, louder. Beat: found family assembling under fire.

chapters.title: Siege of Light
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. The strike team breaches Vell. Zephyrine uploads the confession into himself—the only secure channel left—as the station's systems fail around him. Beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Through the dreaming children, the confession pours into every mind in orbit—Meridian, Combine, everyone—at once. Vasquez holds the docking ring; Amara shields the kids; Zephyrine nearly burns out carrying the signal. Beat: catharsis through connection.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Bombardment orders dissolve mid-transmission. Officers refuse commands; the war machine stalls against ten thousand simultaneous witnesses. Beat: stunned, fragile silence.

chapters.title: Justice, Informal
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV. No court convenes; none is needed. The named conspirators are arrested by their own subordinates. Zephyrine realizes the case inherited from a dead man is finally closed—not by law, but by people. Beat: hard-won peace.

chapters.title: The Quiet Dream
chapters.summary: Mira's POV. The shared dream fades to warmth, then silence. She visits Zephyrine at the docks—not carrier and message now, just family. Beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: Vector Forward
chapters.summary: Zephyrine POV, closing. He takes a new contract: hauling the children of both sides home from evacuated stations. The original's ghost feels less like a debt and more like a hand on his shoulder. Beat: earned hope, forward motion.
